Description: Uncovered a JSON Web Token, which may lead to unauthorized access to web applications and sensitive user data.
Author: Ayberk Arda
Message:
feat(db): normalise nutrition plans and close the plan-column cutover

Nutrition plans followed workout plans out of profiles.nutrition_plan and into
nutrition_plans and nutrition_plan_meals, with reads and writes switched in the
same change.

No structural parsing was attempted. The items field is free text in two
dialects — "Yulaf:80, Tavuk:200" in one place and "Yulaf Ezmesi 80g\nTavuk
200g" in another — and inferring meals or macros from either would be
invention. One row per day holds the original text verbatim plus the existing
kcal total, so the round trip is exact for both dialects; the position column
is present but always zero, reserved for real meal granularity later. A
non-integer or negative total stores NULL rather than rounding, because
rounding would lose data silently and break the round-trip guarantee.

As with workout plans, a single SQL function is shared by the migration and
the save RPC so the two paths cannot drift, and save_nutrition_plan rewrites a
client's active plan atomically under RLS.

ADR 0014 records a deliberate departure from the plan's rule that only the
coach writes to plan tables: the client can save their own nutrition plan
today, because nutrition has no approval flow like workouts do. Enforcing the
rule literally would have removed a working feature without anyone noticing.
The accepted cost — the client can overwrite what the coach set, with no audit
trail — is written down, along with the condition for revisiting it.

Applies upfront the two lessons from the workout cutover, which were only
caught afterwards there: the coach drawer's nutrition editor would have become
a silent no-op write and is removed in favour of the Beslenme tab, and the
client's profile page would have kept reading the deprecated column. Both are
now covered by end-to-end tests.

Also closes an environment trap that cost time twice: .env.local points at the
hosted project and NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined at build time, so Playwright's own
build bound the app to the remote database and every login failed. The
webServer block now defaults to the local stack, overridable from the
environment, and the built bundle is verified to contain no hosted project
reference.

Removes what the cutover orphaned: planUpdateSchema, useUpdateProfile,
parseNutritionPlan and the stale comments pointing at the deprecated columns.
Both columns stay populated but unread as a rollback net; their DROP belongs to
the Phase 2 gate.

Test coverage: 19 transform scenarios, 35 RLS scenarios, 226 unit tests and 21
end-to-end tests.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Ayberk Arda
Message:
git status: 8 değişmiş, 32 silinmiş, 69 yeni. Değişen izlenen dosyalar: .gitignore, README.md, eslint.config.mjs, next.config.mjs, package.json, package-lock.json, postcss.config.mjs, src/app/globals.css.

Verified end to end: lint, type-check, format, 180 unit tests, production build,
ruff, mypy --strict, 63 backend tests at 92% coverage, a Docker image smoke test,
9 tables with 37 RLS policies proven to isolate rows, and 28 Playwright E2E tests
across desktop and mobile profiles.

Also fixes: email sign-in was disabled entirely by a mis-set Supabase auth key;
CSP blocked the local Supabase stack, making local development impossible;
rest-day detection matched "Pazar" inside "Pazartesi"; the backend Docker image
could not build at all due to a readme/dockerignore conflict.
